title: Gas from two fitted ASASSN-14ko drag orbits needs further angular momentum transfer to power reference flares
abstract: We test whether gas intercepted in two published ASASSN-14ko drag orbits can power flares through local collision mixing and cooling without further angular momentum export. At one solar mass and unit drag coefficient, positive axial angular momentum keeps bound gas outside 65 gravitational radii. A generous radiation ceiling, including all source collision heat, falls below a 2e50 erg reference flare by at least a factor of 17.5 per orbit. Unlimited storage and convex mixing over 35 orbits still leave energy deficits of factors 17.20 and 16.48. Bound entry into 10 gravitational radii requires export of at least 61 percent of the axial angular momentum. This is a conditional test of two fitted gas inventories, not new telescope evidence or a rejection of drag. Further torque, extra fuel or external energy can evade it. We provide the proof, source replay, synthetic tables, code and independent numerical checks.
